title: Majority Element
statement:
Given an array `nums` of size `n`, find the majority element. The majority element is the element that appears more than `⌊n / 2⌋` times.

You may assume that the majority element always exists in the array.

examples.explanation: 3 appears twice in a 3-element array, which is more than ⌊3 / 2⌋ = 1 time.
2 appears 4 times in a 7-element array, which is more than ⌊7 / 2⌋ = 3 times.

editorial.approach: Use Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm. Initialize `candidate` and `count = 0`. Iterate through the array: if `count === 0`, set `candidate = nums[i]`. Increment `count` if `nums[i] === candidate`, else decrement `count`. The candidate is the majority element.

hints: You can sort the array. If a majority element exists, it will always be at index `n / 2`.
Alternatively, track counts in a hash map. But there is an O(n) time and O(1) space algorithm.
Look up Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm. Keep a candidate and a balance counter.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Sort the array in non-decreasing order. The majority element must reside at index `Math.floor(nums.length / 2)`.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Use Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm. We maintain a candidate element and a count. We increment or decrement the count depending on whether we match the candidate. If the count hits 0, we select the current element as a new candidate.

interviewExplanation: Sorting the array takes O(n log n) time. A Hash Map count takes O(n) space. By using Boyer-Moore Voting, we can identify the majority element in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space by canceling out non-matching elements.
